correctness.rationale: Strict moment log-convexity establishes a single norm-attaining monomial for the scaled backward shift, and a strict contraction on the adjoint positive-degree subspace. Exterior domination produces a rational Schur function Phi with f=Phi(T)g. Exact Schur defect factorization and equality force its Schur tail U to attain norm 1 on a strict contraction; maximum modulus then forces U to be unimodular constant. This yields precisely the affine pairs; direct squared-modulus comparison proves the converse. Norm normalizations, complete quantifiers and atomic boundary are explicitly handled. A supplementary checker passes exact examples, not infinite certification.

value.rationale: The sharp inequality invites a complete extremal-pair classification. Earlier classification required monotone weights; this result removes that substantial and natural restriction, ruling out nonlinear extremizers for peaked Gamma and thin-annulus weights where moment-measure methods are unavailable. The strict Schur-contraction argument gives a structural mechanism and useful starting point for nontrivial near-equality stability questions, though no stability estimate is claimed.
